thread.title: 3 Ways Apple Can Boost Its Stock Price, According to an Analyst

title: 3 Ways Apple Can Boost Its Stock Price, According to an Analyst

organizations.name: ways apple can boost its stock price

text:
3 Ways Apple Can Boost Its Stock Price, According to an Analyst By Updated Jan. 2, 2019 10:17 a.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Greg Baker/AFP/Getty Images Text size
RBC Capital Markets says Apple (ticker: AAPL) can help its beleaguered stock price this year with several different actions.
The firm’s analyst Amit Daryanani reaffirmed his Outperform rating for Apple stock, citing its strong cash position and valuation.
“The main focus on AAPL over the last couple of months has been around soft iPhone unit demand and to the extent that this could disappoint,” he wrote on Wednesday. “We think that in an increasingly ‘risk-off’ environment, AAPL with its strong balance sheet, aggressive buyback, and ability to drive GM’s [gross margins] higher remains a core large-cap tech holding.”
Daryanani has a $220 price target for Apple shares, implying about 43% upside from the current price. Apple stock was down 2.1% on Wednesday to $154.38. Its shares have declined nearly 30% since the end of October as concerns have mounted about weak demand for the iPhone models released last fall.
The analyst listed three things Apple could do to “shake up” its stock.
First, Daryanani said the company could simplify its product portfolio given that consumers haven’t seemed to appreciate the iPhone XR. He said Apple could also be “more aggressive” with leasing financing for iPhones.
The analyst also noted Apple could launch a new content-streaming service that may be bundled with its Apple Music service.
Finally, he believes the company could change its capital allocation program to overweight more dividends over share buybacks.
Apple stock currently has a 1.9% dividend yield, according to FactSet.
Perhaps there are other ways Apple can improve its offerings.
Last month, Barron’s suggested that Apple may want to offer an all-in-one hardware and software subscription offering to stabilize annual revenue and appease investor concern over the cyclical nature of iPhone product launches.
A couple of weeks ago, Barron’s also put Apple stock on its Top 10 Stock Picks for 2019 list, citing its attractive valuation.
